title: GPU adoption mix - reserve vs spot phased plan 2026-2028
summary: Quarterly capacity forecast that splits planned GPU additions between reserved commitments and spot/ephemeral capacity across NA, EU, and APAC. Emphasis on staged rollouts to match model-onboarding cadence and to keep cost-per-token within budgeted thresholds while preserving a 15–25% operational buffer.
primary_objective: Provide a repeatable, region-by-region procurement and activation plan that optimizes for cost while meeting inferred latency and throughput SLAs for host and dedicated customers through 2028.
key_assumptions: Model growth: +42% aggregate token throughput year-over-year driven by new multimodal customers and embedding-heavy workloads
Mix shift: 30% of requests will move to latency-sensitive routes requiring <120ms tail P95; those routes favor reserved capacity
Spot market volatility: estimated 18% preemption rate in APAC spot pools during peak months
Vendor lead times: reserved GPU procurement lead = 10-14 weeks for cloud reserved instances and 6-10 weeks for long-term committed host agreements
Utilization target window: 60-78% steady-state utilization for reserved pools to balance cost and headroom

cost_mix_analysis: Weighted average cost per GPU-hour: reserved = baseline*0.65, spot = baseline*0.28 (after preemption and reprovisioning), effective blended rate modeled per region
NA: prefers reserved mix due to high enterprise demand and lower spot reliability; expected blended GPU-hour $X (see linked forecast sheet)
EU: balanced approach for regulatory customers; reserved ratio higher for EU-customer segments requiring data isolation
APAC: higher spot reliance early reduces OPEX but increases operational complexity and requires extra buffer
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: spot preemptions spike during vendor maintenance windows. Mitigation: implement checkpoint-based recovery + reserve fallback pools for critical routes
Risk: procurement lead times slip. Mitigation: keep rolling 8-week contract option and short-term reserved offers with flexible start dates
Risk: utilization overshoot causing degraded latency. Mitigation: throttle non-critical routes and enable aggressive prefix caching
Risk: regional pricing changes. Mitigation: maintain vendor scorecard and 30-day re-eval window for mix adjustments
